newsitem.title: KUWAIT: U.S.-Kuwait venture gets loan for complex.
newsitem.headline: U.S.-Kuwait venture gets loan for complex.

text.p: Fifty-four Western, Arab and Asian banks and financial institutions on Sunday agreed to lend $1.2 billion to a U.S.-Kuwaiti joint venture to build a petrochemical complex in the Gulf state.

"Today marks the end of a long financial journey," Charles Kline, president of the venture called Equate told the signing ceremony in Kuwait. "Equate should produce its first pounds of product in late July or early August 1997."

Equate, a venture between America's Union Carbide Corp, Kuwait's Petrochemical Industries Company (PIC) and Kuwait's Bubiyan Petrochemical Company, signed the loan agreement with a syndicate of banks assembled mainly by Kuwaiti and American financial institutions.

Bankers said the loan package was designed by Kuwait's largest commercial bank, National Bank of Kuwait (NBK), which has described the loan as the largest non-recourse financing ever arranged in the Gulf outside of the Gulf's crude oil and refinery sector.
The package is also the first major loan in the Gulf to combine conventional and Islamic financing, they said.
The total project cost is $2 billion. The non-debt protion will come from the partners' equity participation.
The interest rate is priced at 1.625 percent above London interbank offered rate (Libor) if the project is completed by September 30, 1998, and 1.875 percent above Libor thereafter, bankers said.
The agreement also entails a commitment fee of 0.5 percent, they said. The loan was heavily oversubscribed.

The plant, which will be one of the Gulf's largest petrochemical plants, will make 650,000 tonnes a year of ethylene, 450,000 tonnes a year of polyethylene and 350,000 tonnes a year of ethylene glycol.

The statement said the loan was arranged by Arab Banbking Corporation, Saudi-based Arab Petroleum Investments Corporation (APICORP), Chase Manhattan Bank, Citibank, Bahrain-based Gulf International Bank GIOH.BH, Kuwait-based Gulf Investment Corporation (GIC), JP Morgan, Kuwait Finance House and (NBK).
These banks will also underwtrite the loan with al-Ahli Bank of Kuwait, Saudi-based Arab Investment Company, Burgan Bank, Commercial Bank of Kuwait and Gulf Bank of Kuwait, the statement said.
The loan has two tranches -- $500 million over 10-1/2 years for Kuwaiti institutions and $700 million over 8-1/2 years for Gulf-based and international institutions.
